## Findings refused (no change), with reason

- **Flag 1, `"Ede` unclosed (unit 24).** Kept the drafter's reading: narration, no quote supplied. Reading it as Chinggis's speech would put "Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun" (unit 25) in his own mouth; Shiratori's opening mark is simply unclosed. The convention (supply missing *opening* marks) does not cover a missing *closing* mark. Only the "cannot" in the note was softened (#14).
- **Flag 2, §202 subjects.** "they" in units 0–1 and the passive/impersonal subjects elsewhere are hedged in the notes; the grammar gives no subject, and the Ming do not either. Accepted.
- **Flag 3, grouping of peoples and commanders (units 18–20).** The Ming do not join the numbers to the names; the drafter's reading (three thousands Ongirad, two Ikires, five Önggüd) is one of several and is said to be so. Only the punctuation of `i` and the §182 parallel were touched (#10, #11). Whether Alaqu-Šidigid and Quri-Küregen are one man is left undecided, as the Ming give two.
- **Flag 4, Shigi-Qutuqu's speech joins (units 31–40).** Checked: opening mark at idx 219, closing at 286; `i` quote marks balance (opened in 31, closed in 40); each unit break falls on Shiratori's full stops or a clean clause end. The "than whom" questions were left as a rhetorical pair.
- **Flag 5, inferred stems.** moγaγ̇a- ('expose', Ming 白), keseġü- ('punish', Ming 懲戒), iriče-, ki-: ki- is attested in the glossary (#16); iriče- brought to the glossary's hiriče- (#27); moγaγ̇a- and keseġü- stay hedged in their notes (stem uncertain), which is honest, and are not in the glossary — the glosser should mark them uncertain. Chinggis's speeches (units 42–44, 45–49, 50–51, 53–57) have the right speaker: the second person is Shigi-Qutuqu throughout.
- **Flag 6, 'earth-walled towns' (unit 60).** Kept: 土 墻有的 (城)子 gives it word for word; only the 'me/something' additions were removed.
- **Flag 7, speaker of the reply (unit 61).** Kept as Chinggis: after a petition (öčižüġü) the answer comes from the one petitioned, and the next unit names Shigi-Qutuqu afresh as subject, which marks the switch.
- **Flag 8, gür.** The adjective reading 'all, whole' (Ming 普) is right in every use; the existing glossary entry gür is the name Gür (Gür Qan). The glosser must broaden the entry (old entry whole + " · " + 'all, whole, universal (adjective; Ming 普)'), not overwrite it.
- **Flag 9, edition slips.** Sigi-Qutoqu-jin (unit 55) and Ming 做第 for 做弟 (unit 39) are correctly noted and left as printed; the Han 汪古敦 against -ü (unit 19) now also noted (#11). `t` unchanged in all cases.
- **Passives in `i` for unnamed agents** (unit 9 "were appointed and named", unit 38–39 "I was made to lie", unit 40 "is given"): defensible English for an unmarked agent, and each is said to be so in the note. Left.
- **Münkö (unit 14) against Münggügür, Ünggiran etc.** The ṅ → ng rule is not applied to Müṅkö or the house Münlig; left to follow Münlig (house). Huildar → "Quildar" follows the house name.
- **žarliγ bolurun `l` "being-when"** against the morph 'becoming': the house `l` style; left.
- **Unit 0 note "1206 … by the usual reckoning".** A date from outside the text, but flagged as such; left.
- **Morph entries**: all other lemmas and glosses were checked against the form and the Ming gloss (including -ldu-, -lča-, -γsad, -γsen, -leġe, -žüġü, -küi, -tala/-tele, -tan/-ten, the reflexive-possessives, -ji / -i / -a / -e / -dur / -eče / -ača / -ijar / -ġer) and found sound.

## Remaining doubts for pass 2 / the glosser

- Alaqu-Šidigid, Quri-Küregen: one man or two (units 19; #11).
- Whose "own foot / own side" (units 38–39): the agent is unnamed; passive kept.
- Shigi-Qutuqu-jin na-dur ejetüžü (unit 55): genitive consulter, joining uncertain.
- ögümü (unit 40): present, interrogative or passive?
- The glossary will need new entries or broadening for: gür (adjective), hisgei/isgei/toγ̇urγa/joγ̇urγa, hiriče- (iriče-), keseġü-, moγaγ̇a-, urγu-, gedki-, igeġe-, žügle-, ejetü-, -tuγai after alda-, -dekün/-daqun (passive + participle), tusa 'service' (Ming 恩), the names. The existing `ki-`, `neke-`, `čaγ̇ura-`, `uri-`, `öči-` entries cover this part's use.

# Review, pass 2 — secret-history-202-203

Reviewer: adversarial second pass over `gloss.json` (every entry against the text of `units.json` and the Ming gloss in the packet: dictionary form, meaning, grammar label, bracket) and a second read of `units.json`; both edited in place by script (valid JSON). Structure confirmed: 64 units, 450 words, every `t` identical to the packet's romanized words for its run of indices (unchanged from pass 1), `ln`/`p` untouched, gloss keys = `novel-forms.json` keys (156) + the one `__broaden__`. No modern translation was opened or recalled.

Checks run by script: (a) every `[bracket]` in every gloss entry equals the packet's Ming gloss for that token (whitespace and U+FE00 ignored): all 156 pass; (b) every `[bracket]` inside a unit morph is a part of the Ming gloss of its word: 9 failures, fixed below; (c) every English name in a gloss entry appears in the `i` of its unit: all agree; (d) morph lemmas of the 175 known forms agree with the existing glossary's dictionary forms: all agree; (e) `__broaden__` gür: old entry whole + " · " + new: confirmed.

Totals: 17 changes. Critical 0 · major 0 · moderate 4 · minor 13.

## Changes — gloss.json

| # | key | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 4 | aldaγ̇uldaqun, aldaγ̇ul | minor | alda- glossed "to be fined" here and "to incur a penalty" in aldatuγai (same stem, three wordings) | All three: "to incur a penalty, to offend (Ming 罰)"; the matching unit-51 morph glosses brought into line |

## Findings refused (no change), with reason

- **-žüġü / -žuγ̇u / -leġe labels** ("past tense" vs "past narrative tense"): the existing glossary uses both labels for these suffixes; left.
- **Muqali-tan "collective"** (units 31, 63) against "plural possessive 'those having'" for -tan elsewhere: the existing glossary entry muqali-tan has 'and the like, and others'; same Ming 等. Left.
- **Date 1206 in unit 0**: from outside the text but flagged in the note as the usual reckoning (pass 1). Left.
- **Passives in `i`** (units 30, 38–40): see pass 1; unmarked agents.
- **`l` colons/commas added** (e.g. unit 18 "Uṅgirad: Butu-Küregen"): `l` is a rendering, not a transcript; left.
- **urira "converb of purpose"** and **ögümü**, **qubilaldu**: labelled uncertain where the grammar is uncertain; no better label from the text.
- **bürün in unit 24** is not rendered in `i` ("being"): absorbed by the converb chain; the `l` has it. Left.

## Remaining doubts

- Whether the existing glossary entries should be broadened for this part's uses (the build allows one `__broaden__` here, so only gür was done): ger (Ming 房, entry has 家 / 室), edüi (Ming 這些, entry 只這般), hüleġü (Ming 多, entry 多餘), iretügei (with an accusative, Ming 敎來者), kürtele (Ming 直到, entry 到了). Their bracket differs from the Ming at this place; the glosser may wish to add them.
- Alaqu-Šidigid / Quri-Küregen: one man or two (unchanged from pass 1).
- Genitive consulter Shigi-Qutuqu-jin na-dur ejetüžü (unit 55); ögümü (unit 40); ambar (unit 40), as in pass 1.
- The English `i` for units 38–39 ("his own") leaves the referent unnamed, as does the Mongol.
